ChatGPT's latest update adds a Mac integration: it can handle conversations from Apple's "Messages" app. This feature corresponds to iMessage, SMS, and RCS.

The Mac version of ChatGPT now has an Apple "Messages" plugin

The new Apple "Messages" plugin allows ChatGPT to read and search chat history on Mac, and to prepare and send messages. OpenAI says this feature is available to all tiers of the ChatGPT macOS desktop app, and also supports ChatGPT Work and Codex.

This kind of access raises concerns about privacy and control, so OpenAI emphasises that, by default, sending messages requires user approval. Users should think carefully before granting long-term approval. OpenAI's plugin guidelines detail the related risks, how to revoke permissions, and a known issue involving a task that disables approval prompts.

Currently, this feature is only available on Macs with Apple silicon; Intel models are not yet supported.

More features such as collaborative editing on sites and sharing conversation snapshots

Although the "Messages" plugin is the most eye-catching new feature for Apple users, this update also includes several other improvements. For example, pinned conversations can now stay in sync between the ChatGPT desktop and iOS apps, so users can access important conversations anytime on Mac and iPhone.

ChatGPT now also lets users share read-only snapshots of local Codex conversations. These snapshots will not change as the original conversation is updated.

Links generated from personal accounts can be accessed by anyone with the URL; links from a workspace are limited to members of that workspace. OpenAI says Codex will redact known sensitive formats, but reminds users to review the snapshots, as they may still contain sensitive information.

Beyond that, site owners can invite active members of the same workspace to co-edit sites that support collaboration. Editors can update content and database data, save versions, and publish changes after the owner has completed the first publish. Owners retain control over access, settings, analytics, and version restoration.

Some site owners can also change the URL hosted by ChatGPT without redeploying, and the old URL will automatically redirect to the new one.

Finally, the "computer use history" feature launched last week will be expanded to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK. This opt-in feature requires the "memory" feature to be turned on and remains off by default.

You can see the full announcement of this update here.
